definition: A push or pull that one body exerts on another as they interact; a vector, measured in newtons (N), where $\pu{1 N} = \pu{1 kg m s-2}$.
The vector sum of all the forces acting on a body: the single force with the same effect as all of them together, also called the net force.
A body stays at rest, or keeps moving at constant velocity, unless a resultant force acts on it.
The resultant force on a body equals its rate of change of momentum; for a body of constant mass this becomes $F = ma$.
If body A exerts a force on body B, then B exerts a force on A that is equal in size, opposite in direction and of the same type; the two forces act on different bodies.
